The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. Plans have been submitted to turn a historic outbuilding beside a Grade I listed building into a five-bedroom home. Mick Hilless has applied to Huntingdonshire District Council to turn a barn and office building linked to Bodsey House into a home on Bodsey Toll Road, Ramsey. Bodsey House is Grade I listed, meaning it is of exceptional interest. The property was once a 13th-century hermitage belonging to Ramsey Abbey but has since been altered and turned into a family home. The plans would turn the barn and office building at the rear of the site into one five-bedroom home. The historic barn is curtilage listed, which means it is legally protected as it sits within the grounds of a listed building. Documents by Scroxton Architects say the barn and office building are dilapidated and no longer suitable for modern agricultural or commercial use. The plans would demolish the modern open-sided portal barn at the rear and replace it with a two-storey extension forming a five-bedroom home. The site is about 1.8km north-east of Ramsey and covers 0.2 hectares. rawItems.title: Motorcyclist injured after crash with van on busy Cambs road
rawItems.content: A motorcyclist has been injured in a crash with a van on a busy Cambridgeshire road. Police were called to Oilmills Road, Pondersbridge, near Ramsey and Whittlesey, at around 8pm on Monday September 28. A spokesperson for Cambridgeshire Constabulary said a motorcyclist suffered minor injuries after a collision with a van. No arrests were made.
